title: Bites & Stings
summary: Watch every bite or sting for a severe allergic reaction. Snakebite: keep still and get help. Animal bites: wash well and get medical advice.

callEmergency.headline: Call {EMERGENCY} for these bites and stings
when: Signs of anaphylaxis: breathing difficulty, swelling of face or throat, collapse
Stings inside the mouth or throat, or many stings
Serious animal bites with heavy bleeding

steps.title: Watch for anaphylaxis
steps.text: If they have breathing difficulty, swelling of face or throat, or feel faint, treat as anaphylaxis now.

steps.title: Bee and wasp stings
steps.text: Remove a bee sting quickly by any means (scrape or pull). Apply a cold pack. Watch for allergic reactions for at least 30 minutes.

steps.title: Snakebite
steps.text: Call {EMERGENCY}. Keep them calm and still, with the bitten limb still. Remove rings and tight items from the limb. Note the time and, if safe, the snake's appearance – do not try to catch it.
points: Pressure immobilisation bandaging is only recommended for certain snakes and regions – follow local protocol

steps.title: Animal and human bites
steps.text: Control bleeding, then wash the wound well with soap and plenty of running water. Cover it. Seek medical advice – infection, tetanus and rabies risk need assessing.

steps.title: Ticks
steps.text: Grasp the tick close to the skin with fine-tipped tweezers and pull steadily straight out. Clean the area. Note the date and watch for rash or fever.

warningSigns: Breathing difficulty or swelling of face/throat
doNot: Snakebite: do not cut, suck, apply ice, apply a tourniquet, or try to catch the snake
Do not squeeze a tick's body or burn it
Do not ignore animal bites – rabies risk needs assessing
